classification.difficultyReason: Reduce the spherical cap to a circular cross-section, identify the half-chord and radius-minus-height distance, then solve the familiar Pythagorean model.

content.prompt: A spherical buoy is floating so that its visible cap has height $10\text{ cm}$ and diameter $30\text{ cm}$. Find the radius of the buoy.

spec.description: Editable circular cross-section; the waterline chord separates the visible upper cap from the submerged portion. Cap height and full chord diameter are retained. Source texture and coloured fills are omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal waterline chord has length 30 cm; its midpoint-to-top distance is 10 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two supplied measurements are shown.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{65}{4}\text{ cm}$

Use the half-chord $15\text{ cm}$ and centre-to-waterline distance $r-10$ in Pythagoras.
answer.worked:
Consider the circular cross-section. Let its radius be $r\text{ cm}$. The perpendicular from the centre bisects the waterline chord, so the half-chord is $15\text{ cm}$ and the centre-to-waterline distance is $(r-10)\text{ cm}$. By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}(r-10)^2+15^2&=r^2\\r^2-20r+325&=r^2\\20r&=325\\r&=\frac{65}{4}.\end{align*}$$
The radius of the buoy is $\dfrac{65}{4}\text{ cm}$.
